article.content: Pool A: Jillaroos 78-0 England Australia run in 15-tries-to-none in one-sided contest at HBF Park The Jillaroos sent a reminder to English rugby league that it is losing touch with the best in the world with a 78-0 hammering in Perth. article.aiArticle:
Australia's women's rugby league team delivered an emphatic reminder of their global dominance on Friday, routing England **78-0** in a heavily lopsided Pool A encounter at Perth's **HBF Park**. According to a report by *Sport | The Guardian*, the reigning champions overwhelmed their opponents by running in an astonishing **15 tries to none**. The comprehensive shutout left English rugby league facing difficult questions about how far the nation has fallen behind the international benchmark.

## A One-Sided Affair in Perth

From the opening whistle, the contest belonged entirely to the Australian side, widely known as the Jillaroos. English defenders struggled constantly to contain the relentless attacking waves, eventually conceding **15 tries** over the course of the **80 minutes**. The sheer scale of the **78-0** scoreline highlights a widening competitive chasm between the Southern Hemisphere powerhouse and the northern contenders. For a full breakdown of how the action unfolded, readers can revisit our live commentary on the [Australia 78-0 England: women’s Rugby League World Cup – as it happened](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/australia-england-womens-rugby-league-world-cup-match-report) page.

The match served as the latest installment in a history of difficult fixtures for the English side against the green and gold. Following the final whistle, the defeat was immediately categorized by observers as yet another chapter in a grim sequence of heavy losses. Further examination of this ongoing trend can be found in our retrospective coverage detailing how this [poor England suffer another Australia humiliation](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/australia-england-womens-rugby-league-world-cup-match-report). 

## Tournament Structure Under Fire

Beyond the raw numbers on the scoreboard, the aftermath of the fixture triggered fierce debate over the organization of the international tournament itself. In the wake of the defeat, English camp figures voiced sharp criticism regarding the competition's design, pointing to structural flaws as a contributing factor to the squad's perilous standing. Readers interested in the administrative fallout can explore our analysis of why [McDermott blames Rugby League World Cup format as England face exit](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/australia-england-womens-rugby-league-world-cup-match-report). 

The Rugby League World Cup brings together top international federations every few years, though the international calendar has historically struggled to provide regular, competitive fixtures for emerging European nations outside of domestic European championships. 

## The Stakes and Broader Impact

Context: Blowout results of this magnitude threaten to undermine the commercial and competitive appeal of international women's rugby league, potentially stalling the global growth of the sport. While the Jillaroos continue to showcase an exceptionally high standard of athleticism and tactical execution, the lack of parity affects broadcasters, sponsors, and players alike. For England, repeated heavy setbacks risk eroding player morale and domestic investment just as the women's game fights for broader mainstream traction.

What to watch: Analysts will be monitoring how the English coaching staff reorganizes the squad for their upcoming survival matches, alongside any potential intervention or schedule reviews from tournament organizers addressing competitive imbalances.

Sources: [Sport | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/24/australia-england-womens-rugby-league-world-cup-match-report)
